cards.title: Two ways to apply it
cards.body: Contact discharge touches conductive metal. Air discharge approaches a surface that will not take the contact tip until a spark jumps. Contact is the repeatable one. Air moves with humidity, speed, and shape.

cards.title: The familiar levels
cards.body: The usual IEC 61000-4-2 table is contact 2, 4, 6, and 8 kV, and air 2, 4, 8, and 15 kV. The product standard picks the level. 'Level X' means the product standard has to fill it in. Do not invent one.

cards.title: What a radio standard actually requires
cards.body: EN 301 489-1 clause 9.3 sets ±4 kV contact and ±8 kV air, and it tells you to include the intermediate levels from EN 61000-4-2. That is level 2 contact and level 3 air, not the top of the basic table.

cards.title: The current waveform
cards.body: At 4 kV contact the familiar calibration is 15 A at the first peak, 8 A at 30 ns, and 4 A at 60 ns. Current scales with voltage, so 8 kV is double and 2 kV is half. The first peak is fast, on the order of 1 ns. A surge's 1.2/50 µs shape is a different test.

cards.title: How many shots
cards.body: Shots are single discharges, not a burst. Try both polarities. Once you know which one hurts, the usual minimum is at least ten shots at each selected point in that polarity. Machine-gunning the trigger is not contact mode.

cards.title: Planes
cards.body: Direct shots go to the product. Indirect shots go to the horizontal coupling plane under it and the vertical coupling plane beside it. The product sits on a thin insulator on the HCP. The usual bleed to the ground reference is two 470 kΩ resistors. Table height is about 0.8 m.

cards.title: What 'pass' means
cards.body: A spark is not a failure by itself. EN 301 489-1 uses the transient criterion: no unintended transmission, no mode change, no loss of critical stored data, and the radio works as intended after the shot. A link that needs a manual reboot has not met that last line.

cards.title: Who gets the test
cards.body: In EN 301 489-1 Table 2, ESD applies to fixed and portable use, not to vehicle use. Vehicle radios take supply pulses from ISO 7637-2 instead. Do not skip ESD on a handheld because a vehicle column exists.

cards.title: Where it fails
cards.body: Shoot seams, screws, and connector shells, not only the middle of a panel. Paint is neither a reliable insulator nor a reliable conductor. A coiled ground lead changes the edge. Skipping the vertical plane skips half of the indirect test.

cards.title: Preview, not the appliance table
cards.body: The CISPR 14-2 file is a preview of appliance immunity. It names Categories I to V and points at the ESD basic standard. It does not define the categories or the levels. Do not treat it as the requirement for a given tool or appliance.
